_meta.purpose: Deterministic sanity bounds for the event-driven scanner modes (pead / filings / gap) once they are pre-simulated by sweep.js. Guards against a corrupt/param-drifted backtest result (trade-count blowup, DD explosion, negative Sharpe) reaching the status page or gating a draft->test->sim-live promotion. Consumed by the ingest/sweep sanity check + qa-check.js (hard fail on breach). Analogue of config/dtx/_sanity-baselines.json.
_meta.scope: SIM-ONLY. Signals + simulated perf only (signals.json -> sweep.js -> gen-status-page -> gen-api). No paper/live/deploying/liquidated concept, no order execution.
_meta.source: SPEC docs/specs/event-driven-scanners.md §4.2. Baselines produced 2026-07-11 by the Backtest-validation agent via mcp__marketdata__* (RunBacktest DSL for gap + appoint-technical for pead; GetInsiderActivity/QueryData event-study for filings). Real MCP data, sim-only, zero fabrication.
_meta.fill_instructions: The Backtest agent replaces each null with the healthy walk-forward baseline (total_trades, max_dd_pct, sharpe, cagr_pct, win_rate) BEFORE promoting the mode past draft. Never invent these numbers — leave null until a real MCP-backed backtest exists (MCP hard-stop, zero fabrication). trades_ratio_high/low are applied to the per-mode total_trades once set (2.2x / 0.4x, generous to tolerate legitimate window extension; DD/sharpe/win_rate/cagr are the primary tripwires).
_meta.universal_note: While a per-mode baseline is null/TBD, only the _universal tripwires apply (|max_dd|>50%, sharpe<0, win_rate outside [15,92], cagr<-5%).
_meta.coverage_caveat: MCP bar history in this environment starts ~2025-04-30 for SPY and most names (deep-history backfill did not extend to the requested 2024-07-01). With the engine's 200-bar warmup, the simulation only produces live trades in 2026 (yearly_stats shows year 2026 only) — effectively ~2026 H1, a slice that contains the Feb–Mar 2026 correction and the June 2026 chop. A genuine per-regime walk-forward (RISK-ON / NEUTRAL / ERO across multiple years) is NOT achievable on this data. All metrics below are honest but low-coverage; treat as provisional, re-run when deeper history is available.
_meta.dsl_corrections: SPEC §2.3/§2.1 pass_expr had two DSL bugs, corrected here: (1) gap_pct() returns a RATIO ((open-prevclose)/|prevclose|), so a 4% gap is gap_pct()>=0.04, NOT >=4 (the literal >=4 demands a 400% gap -> zero trades). (2) close > hhv('high',20) is self-defeating because hhv includes the current bar (today's high is in the window, so close can't exceed it) -> zero trades; replaced with close >= hhv('close',20) (a genuine 20-day closing-high breakout). SPEC should be patched to match.

_benchmark.note: Peak 695.49 (2026-01-27) -> trough 631.97 (2026-03-30) = -9.1%. This is the bar a mode must beat to be promoted (spec §4.1).

pead._verdict: STAY DRAFT. No positive evidence. The appoint-technical proxy (gap_pct()>=0.03 && close>ema20 && vol>1.5M) came back NEGATIVE (sharpe -0.06, total_return -1.5%, max_dd 59.7%) — it fails the universal sharpe>=0 floor, so it is deliberately NOT recorded as a healthy baseline. The guidance-qualified event-study (the actual PEAD edge) could not be run cleanly: earnings_quarterly returns fiscal-quarter labels (2Q2025 …), not actual print dates, and bar history is ~14 months, so D+5/D+20 drift on a beat+guidance-up cohort is not computable without a print-date map. Do not promote.
pead._validation: Earnings-beat cohort event-study (beat + guidance up + gap held) drift D+5/D+20>0, TP1 win-rate>55% in RISK-ON, + appoint technical RunBacktest (spec §2.1/§4.1).

_appoint_technical_proxy.note: Recorded for transparency ONLY — this is gap-up-in-uptrend WITHOUT the beat/guidance filter that defines PEAD; it is NOT the mode baseline and FAILS the universal sharpe floor.

filings._status: DRAFT — UNEXPLOITABLE COVERAGE (kept null; only universal tripwires apply)
filings._verdict: STAY DRAFT. Event-study inexploitable, not flattered. GetInsiderActivity(days=180, direction=buy) over the default SP500 large-cap universe (200 symbols) returned net insider BUYING in only 3 names (ADSK, HUM, RBA). Applying the cluster rule (>=2 distinct insiders, code P, <=30d): only ADSK qualifies (CAHILL/Dir $378k 06-23, Anagnost/CEO $498k 06-16, Moorjani/CFO $494k 06-15). HUM = 1 buyer; RBA = same insider twice. Cohort n≈1 -> no statistically meaningful D+20 drift baseline. Insider cluster-buy is a small/mid-cap phenomenon; the default universe (SP500) structurally misses it. A real baseline needs a small/mid-cap symbol scan with deeper history. Flags leg (anti-dilution) is a non-regression check, not a return baseline.
filings._validation: Insider cluster-buy (code P, >=2 insiders) event-study drift D+20>0 (US-only); flags leg validated by non-regression (avoided dilution stops). NOT a RunBacktest DSL signal (spec §2.2/§4.1).

_cohort_evidence.note: US-only by construction (no EU PDMR feed, spec §2.2).

gap._verdict: STAY DRAFT. This is the cleanest of the three (pure DSL) and produced a valid backtest that passes the universal sanity floor, so its metrics are recorded as the drift-detection baseline. But it does NOT meet the promotion gate (spec §4.1): total_return +10.5% << SPY buy-and-hold +34.5% over the same window, and raw-equity max_dd 29.8% >> the 8% ceiling (driven by the June-2026 cluster: 13 trades, 23% win, -28.5% that month). CAVEAT: RunBacktest applies the engine's DEFAULT exit logic, not the scanner's actual clamped 3–8% stop + R/R-gate + regime filter, so the mode's realized DD would differ — this backtest bounds signal expectancy/frequency, not the mode's true risk. Not promotable on current evidence + coverage.
gap._validation: RunBacktest DSL walk-forward per regime; must beat SPY buy-and-hold with max_dd<=8% (spec §2.3/§4.1).
